findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32) despite all image handling being user-initiated single-file selection via <input type="file" accept="image/*"> — logo upload, stamp upload, and receipt scanning. TargetSdk=35 makes this a no-op on API 33+, but the broad storage permission is still in the manifest and is unnecessary since the WebView file chooser does not require it.
findings.evidence: Manifest: READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 with maxSdkVersion=32. WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 with maxSdkVersion=28. requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11. Photo usage: SettingsModal.tsx:64 (logo upload, accept="image/*"), SettingsModal.tsx:134 (stamp upload, accept="image/*"), FinanceManager.tsx:267 (receipt scan, accept="image/*" capture="environment"). App is Biz-flow.cloud (business finance app), NOT a dedicated media manager.
findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permissions from AndroidManifest.xml — the app's image selection flows use <input type="file"> which invokes the system file picker without requiring broad storage permissions on any modern Android version. Remove requestLegacyExternalStorage="true". No functional impact since all image operations are user-initiated and single-file.

findings.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32), WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=28), and uses requestLegacyExternalStorage=true, but all file operations use Capacitor Filesystem plugin with Directory.Documents (scoped storage on API 30+). No raw file path access found. The permissions are legacy artifacts from pre-scoped-storage era.
findings.evidence: Manifest: requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 (maxSdkVersion=28), READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 (maxSdkVersion=32). main.tsx:31 creates 'Biz-flow/' folder via Capacitor Filesystem mkdir(Directory.Documents). nativeFileService.ts writes/reads PDFs via Capacitor Filesystem to Directory.Documents/Biz-flow/. DocumentShareModal.tsx and useDocumentActions.ts similarly use Capacitor Filesystem scoped API. No direct Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() usage anywhere in the codebase. localStorage reference in assets is browser-level web storage, unrelated to Android file permissions.
findings.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE from AndroidManifest.xml. Remove android:requestLegacyStorage="true" (only applies to API 29, irrelevant on targetSdk=35). The Capacitor Filesystem plugin already uses scoped storage via the SAF on API 30+ and works correctly without these permissions.
